subject: WellPath: sudden 429 spike after project reorg — urgent
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@wellpathhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@wellpathhealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: 429 surge and timeouts in production

Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 429s and client timeouts on our production key this morning around 07:50 PDT. The errors coincide with our morning batch traffic (10:45–11:15 ET) but the error rate is much higher than expected — roughly 30% of requests are getting 429s and many of the retries are compounding. Attaching a small sample of request logs (wellpath-request-logs.txt).

Symptoms:
- 429s from /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints
- Increased p95 latency from ~320ms to >1.2s before timeout
- Customer-facing service degraded (timeouts seen by end users)

We did not change our client-side retry strategy. We suspect something changed on Redwood's side: our engineering team noticed a change to project-level quota assignments in the console last night during a housekeeping task. We need immediate mitigation — can you escalate?

This is impacting patient-facing features; our incident response is active. Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Platform Operations
WellPath Health

Attachment: wellpath-request-logs.txt (text, 48 KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 429 surge and timeouts in production

Anita — thank you, and I'm sorry for the disruption. I have looped in our on-call infra lead (Aditya) and your customer success lead (Hannah). We'll triage immediately.

Short plan for the next 90 minutes:
1) Aditya: confirm whether any org/project quota changes rolled out last night and advise a mitigation (temporary override or rollback).
2) Rishi/Hannah: I'll draft a short customer-facing status update and exec note for WellPath leadership.
3) If we can confirm quota misassignment, we'll apply an emergency override to restore capacity and follow-up with a postmortem and credit discussion.

Please expect a direct phone from me if needed.

—Marissa
VP, Global Sales (Redwood Inference)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@wellpathhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 429 surge and timeouts in production

Anita / team — I pulled the audit logs and traced the spike. Quick summary: an automated migration that applied new "project->org" tier mappings ran at 02:12 UTC last night and mis-assigned WellPath's primary project to the lower throughput tier by mistake. The policy change reduced effective tokens-per-second for that project, which explains the sudden 429s and increased latency due to client retries flooding the limited slots.

What I did (immediate):
- Applied a temporary override raised to the previous throughput tier (manual override) at 08:28 PDT — you should see the error rate begin to drop within a few minutes.
- Collected a quota audit CSV (attached) that shows before/after mappings and the migration job id.

Next steps I recommend:
- Keep the override for 24 hours while we roll back the bad mapping and run a validation job.
- Disable the migration job until we fix the mapping logic.
- We'll run a short replay test to confirm we do not hit the adjusted limits again.

Notes: this is distinct from per-token rate limiting; it's a tier assignment bug at the org->project mapping layer. I will follow with the migration job id and trace.

Attachment: quota_audit.csv (CSV, 26 rows)

—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 429 surge and timeouts in production

Anita — sorry for the interruption. Marissa/Aditya — thanks for the quick response.

Customer comms: I'll send a one-paragraph acknowledgment to WellPath now and follow up with an exec note. Proposed language: "We've identified an internal configuration update that temporarily reduced throughput for your project; we've applied an emergency override and are rolling back the change. We expect normal service within 30 minutes and will schedule a postmortem that includes credits for the downtime." Happy to adjust.

Commercial/credits: per our SLA, this qualifies as a service degradation. I'll prepare an initial credit estimate (TBD) and loop in finance if needed.

—Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts

Team — thank you. Two operational items from Product/Platform side:
1) Rollback plan: disable migration job, revert org->project mapping to previous state, run validation against a staging snapshot. Target: rollback complete within 6 hours.
2) Guardrail change: we need an automated preflight check that detects unusual downstream throughput drops when a tier mapping changes. I'll create a short RFC and push a hotfix to the migration pipeline after scope review.

Hannah/Rishi — can you confirm customer-side acceptance of the temporary override and the timeframe for a postmortem? I'll include the technical timeline in the exec brief.

—Vivek
VP, Product (Redwood Inference)

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: WellPath: sudden 429 spike after project reorg — urgent

Anita —

Quick exec summary for your leadership:
- Incident: automated migration mis-assigned WellPath's primary project to a lower throughput tier, causing elevated 429s and retry amplification.
- Impact window: 2026-10-01 07:50 PDT to 2026-10-01 08:28 PDT (manual override applied).
- Mitigation: manual override applied by Redwood infra at 08:28 PDT; rollback of migration job scheduled and hotfix planned.
- Customer impact: transient service degradation; some end users experienced timeouts during the window. Redwood will provide a detailed postmortem and service credit per SLA.

Follow-ups committed by Redwood:
- Hotfix to migration pipeline and a preflight guard (owner: Vivek; ETA: 2026-10-05).
- Postmortem and credit estimate (owner: Rishi; ETA: 2026-10-04).
- Audit of all recent migration jobs and a pause on automated tier reassignments for customers with active production traffic (owner: Aditya; ETA: 2026-10-02).

Anita — please let us know if you want an on-call conference with our execs; happy to schedule. We appreciate your patience and will keep you updated.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Global Sales
Redwood Inference
